content: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
author: Seneca
story:
The human mind is a master dramatist. It invents catastrophic futures, runs rehearsals for disasters that never happen, and puts us through the emotional misery of tragedies before a single drop of rain has fallen. Seneca warned his friend Lucilius that we torture ourselves far more in our imaginations than in real life.

Most of the monsters we fear live exclusively in our anticipated tomorrows. When challenges actually arrive in the real world, they are usually far more manageable than the phantom terrors we created in our heads.
reflectionPrompt: What worst-case scenario is currently taking up space in your head, and how much actual evidence is there that it is happening today?
